Frey, the god of fertility, summer, sunshine, and prosperity. Originally a giant sent to live among the Aesir, he represents growth, abundance, and the peaceful flourishing of the world. He is a member of the Vanir, the fertility gods who joined the Aesir after a truce between the two divine families.

Frey governs summer, sunshine, and fair weather, and his blessing brings bountiful harvests and prosperous years. He is associated with peace, joy, and sensual pleasure—a gentler face of divinity than the warrior gods Odin and Thor. He rides the golden boar Gullinbursti, whose bristles glow bright enough to light the darkest nights.

His most significant story is one of tragic sacrifice for love. He fell in love with the giantess Gerdr and gave up his magical sword—which fought of its own accord—to win her hand. This sacrifice leaves him weaponless and vulnerable, a weakness that becomes apparent when Ragnarok arrives. He will fight a giant at the end of all things but will do so without his legendary weapon, foreshadowing his death.

Frey shares a connection with his twin sister Freya, also a Vanir deity of fertility and magic. Together they represent the generative forces of the Norse cosmos.
